question: Assume today is 2026-08-15. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in August 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (NPS Visitor Use Statistics). A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times counts as multiple visi
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Visitor Use Statistics program
target.cadence: Monthly, typically published with a lag of several weeks to a few months after the month ends
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-08-15 cutoff; only partial August 2026 data (if any) would be available. The official figure may be revised. The definition counts visits, not unique visitors. Alternative interpretations include total visits (recreation + non-recreation) or vehicle e

candidates.hypothesis: August recreation visits in recent years (e.g., 2023, 2024, 2025) provide a baseline. The 2026 value is likely to be similar to recent August values, adjusted for any known shocks or trends. The relationship is direct: target = recent August value × adjustment factor.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visits for Yellowstone for August 2023, August 2024, and August 2025 (and if available, preliminary August 2026 data or year-to-date 2026 through July). Minimum evidence: at least two recent August values and the most recent July 2026 value to gauge trend.
search_hints: Yellowstone National Park monthly visitation statistics August 2025
NPS visitor use statistics Yellowstone August 2024

candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone's August visits are a share of total NPS August visits or of visits to a comparable set of parks. If NPS-wide August 2026 data or forecasts are available, the share can be applied. Alternatively, nearby parks (Grand Teton, Glacier) may show correlated trends.
candidates.data_to_find: Total NPS recreation visits for August 2025 and any available August 2026 preliminary data; or August visitation for Grand Teton and Glacier for 2023-2025. Minimum evidence: one recent August total for NPS and Yellowstone's share, or comparable park August values.

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle occupancy
candidates.hypothesis: Recreation visits can be estimated from vehicle entries multiplied by average occupancy. If vehicle entry counts for August 2026 are available (even partial), they can be scaled. Historical vehicle counts and occupancy rates provide conversion factors.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone vehicle entry counts for August 2025 (or recent August) and average persons per vehicle. Minimum evidence: one recent August vehicle count and an occupancy estimate. If unavailable, use park-wide traffic counters or entrance station data.

candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays in Yellowstone (lodges, campgrounds) are a component of visits. If occupancy rates and capacity are known for August 2026, they can be converted to visits using average party size and length of stay. This route may only cover overnight visitors, not day visitors.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone lodging and campground capacity, August 2025 occupancy rates, average length of stay, and average party size. Minimum evidence: total overnight capacity and an occupancy rate for August. If unavailable, use Xanterra or park concessioner reports.

candidates.perspective: Park closures, weather, and policy changes
candidates.hypothesis: Any major closures (e.g., road washouts, fires, government shutdown) or policy changes (e.g., reservation requirements) in August 2026 would alter visitation relative to baseline. The direction and magnitude depend on the shock. Historical analogues (e.g., 2022 flood closure) provide adjustment factors.
candidates.data_to_find: News of Yellowstone closures or access restrictions in July-August 2026; any reservation system changes for 2026; weather anomalies. Minimum evidence: confirmation of whether the park was fully open in August 2026 and any known disruptions.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts for Yellowstone or national park tourism in summer 2026 may provide a direct estimate or a growth rate to apply to 2025 August. Prediction markets on total visits or specific thresholds could also be informative.
candidates.data_to_find: Any 2026 summer visitation forecast for Yellowstone from tourism boards, economists, or NPS; prediction market contracts on Yellowstone visits. Minimum evidence: one credible forecast or market price.

candidates.hypothesis: August typically accounts for a stable share of Yellowstone's annual recreation visits (e.g., around 20-25%). If a reliable estimate of total 2026 annual visits exists (from forecasts or year-to-date), the August share can be applied.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone annual recreation visits for 2023-2025 and the August share for those years; any 2026 annual forecast. Minimum evidence: August share for at least two recent years and a 2026 annual estimate.

methods.rationale: Uses the single most recent observed August (2025, p11 = 881,936) as the baseline for August 2026. This is the most direct d1 route: August visitation is highly persistent year to year, and 2025 is the latest August unaffected by the 2026 unknowns. Failure mode: ignores the mild 2026 softness seen in July/YTD and any August-specific shock.

Scales the most recent August value (p11, August 2025 = 881,936) by an assumed August 2026 year-over-year factor (a1). This incorporates the observed 2026 softness (July -2%, YTD -1%) while keeping the August baseline. Shared dependency: both m1 and m2 rest on p11, so they are not independent; m2 adds the 2026 momentum adjustment. Failure mode: if the 2026 softness is July-specific or reverses in August, a1 is wrong.

Averages the three most recent observed August values (2025, 2024, 2021) to smooth year-to-year noise and reduce reliance on a single year. This is a robustness check on m1. Failure mode: 2021 was a record year and may bias the average upward; the three years are not consecutive, so the mean is not a true 3-year average.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Baseline August 2025 (p11) scaled by the 2026 softness factor a1; captures the observed 2026 down-1% to -2% pattern. Shared dependency: p11 is the same NPS series as the target. Failure mode: an August 2026 shock not reflected in a1.
methods.error: input a1: assumption a1 was rejected (target-like: names the target period (2026))

methods.label: m2
methods.rationale: Baseline August 2024 (p12) scaled by a two-year bridge a2; independent of the 2025 August value and robust to a one-year anomaly. Failure mode: a2 misstates the cumulative 2025-2026 change.
methods.error: input a2: assumption a2 was rejected (target-like: names the target period (2026))

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Baseline August 2021 (p13) scaled by a3; uses the record-era August level as an upper anchor. Failure mode: post-2021 demand normalization makes a3 too high.
methods.error: input a3: assumption a3 was rejected (target-like: names the target period (2026))

methods.label: m4
methods.rationale: Mean of the three most recent earlier August values (2025, 2024, 2023) as a simple baseline; ignores the 2026 softness signal but provides a stable central anchor. Failure mode: recent August values may not reflect 2026 conditions.

methods.label: m5
methods.rationale: Scales last August (p11) by the July 2026/July 2025 ratio (p1/p2), transferring the observed July softness to August. Failure mode: July and August shocks differ.

methods.label: m6
methods.rationale: Uses the historical ratio of August visits to YTD-through-August to project August 2026 from the 2026 YTD-through-July level (p4) plus an implied August increment; requires the August/YTD relationship to be stable. Failure mode: 2026 YTD-to-August relationship differs.

rejected.name: August 2026 recreation visits as a fraction of August 2025 recreation visits
rejected.rationale: 2026 YTD through July is down 1% vs 2025 and July 2026 is down 2% vs July 2025; August 2026 likely near or slightly below August 2025, with wide uncertainty for weather, fire, and macro travel conditions.
rejected.applies_when: No major August 2026 closure or demand shock beyond the observed mild 2026 softness.
rejected.falsified_by: Evidence of a major August 2026 closure, fire, or a sharp demand shift.

rejected.name: August 2026 recreation visits as a fraction of August 2024 recreation visits
rejected.rationale: Two-year bridge from the 2024 August level, allowing for the 2025 up-2% and 2026 down-1% to -2% pattern.
rejected.falsified_by: Evidence of a major August 2026 disruption or a large demand shift.

rejected.name: August 2026 recreation visits as a fraction of August 2021 recreation visits
rejected.rationale: 2026 YTD is down 1% vs 2021 and July 2026 is down 11% vs July 2021; August 2026 likely below the 2021 August level but within a wide band.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
